chunks: 2858 - It was narrated from Abū al-Rabīʿ al-Shāmī, who said:
Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام was asked about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
"And [due] to Allah from the people is hajj to the House, for whoever is able to find a way to it."

He said: "What do the people say about it?" It was said to him: "Provision and a mount." He عليه السلام said: "Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام was asked about this, and he said: 'The people would perish, then! If whoever had provision and a mount equal to what sustains his dependents and makes him independent of people were to set out to it and strip them of it, then they would indeed perish.'"

So it was said to him: "Then what is the way?" He said: "Amplitude in wealth: that he performs hajj with part of it while part remains for the sustenance of his dependents. Has not Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made zakat obligatory and only placed it upon one who possesses two hundred dirhams?"

key_terms.اسْتَطَاعَ: had the capability and capacity to undertake it
key_terms.الرَّاحِلَةُ: a riding mount or means of transport
key_terms.الزَّكَاةَ: the obligatory alms-tax used here as an analogy for threshold-based obligation
key_terms.السَّعَةُ: financial sufficiency or amplitude in wealth
key_terms.حِجُّ الْبَيْتِ: the obligation of pilgrimage to the Sacred House
key_terms.سَبِيلًا: a viable means or way, understood here as financial ability
key_terms.عِيَالِهِ: his dependents whose maintenance must remain secured

ai.seo_question: What does "whoever is able to find a way" mean in the verse of hajj obligation?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that the Qur'anic condition of being able to undertake hajj is not merely possessing basic travel provision and a mount. Rather, it means having sufficient wealth to perform hajj while still leaving enough to support one's dependents, showing that financial capacity in Shia fiqh includes preserving the family's necessary maintenance.
